title: Findings (content submitted by the agent via submit_findings)
description: The agent's initial assessment of one alert: answers to the six brief questions as evidence-backed claims, hypothesis status, severity and confidence with separate rationales, justified MITRE techniques, unknowns, alternative explanations and recommended next steps. Containment is only ever a recommendation for analyst consideration (requires_approval: true); nothing is executed. Validated in code against THIS run's evidence (see tools/assessment.py).

account_and_asset.description: Answer to: a. Which account and asset are involved? One object per claim. Every claim cites at least one evidence_ref; anything you cannot cite goes into unknowns instead.

items.description: an evidence_ref exactly as a tool returned it in this run, e.g. wazuh_alerts.jsonl#L64

evidence_refs.description: refs that support this claim (at least one)

timeline.description: Answer to: b. What is the timeline, and which events support the alert? One object per claim. Every claim cites at least one evidence_ref; anything you cannot cite goes into unknowns instead.

items.description: an evidence_ref exactly as a tool returned it in this run, e.g. wazuh_alerts.jsonl#L64

evidence_refs.description: refs that support this claim (at least one)

source_ip_intelligence.description: Answer to: c. What does approved intelligence say about the source IP? (cite the lookup_ip ref and say it is MOCK intel) One object per claim. Every claim cites at least one evidence_ref; anything you cannot cite goes into unknowns instead.

related_events.description: Answer to: d. Are there related events before or after the successful login / key event? One object per claim. Every claim cites at least one evidence_ref; anything you cannot cite goes into unknowns instead.

severity_justification.description: Answer to: e. What severity is justified by evidence? One object per claim, each citing at least one evidence_ref. The second half of question e - what is still unknown - is answered by the top-level unknowns list, never here (a claim without refs is rejected).

evidence_refs.description: refs that support this claim (at least one)

containment.description: Answer to: f. What containment or remediation should a human analyst consider? (for analyst consideration only) One object per claim. Every claim cites at least one evidence_ref; anything you cannot cite goes into unknowns instead.

evidence_refs.description: refs that support this claim (at least one)

hypotheses.description: One entry per hypothesis of the accepted plan (same ids).

id.description: the plan's hypothesis id, e.g. H1

items.description: an evidence_ref exactly as a tool returned it in this run, e.g. wazuh_alerts.jsonl#L64

evidence_refs.description: refs for supported/refuted (at least one); may be [] for undetermined

severity_rationale.description: Why this severity, from the evidence. If it differs from the rubric (docs/severity.md), say so explicitly (mention the rubric) and explain why.

items.description: an evidence_ref exactly as a tool returned it in this run, e.g. wazuh_alerts.jsonl#L64

severity_evidence_refs.description: refs that justify the severity (at least one)

confidence.description: How complete and consistent the evidence is (separate from severity). Never high if a key source failed, timed out or is missing, or sources conflict.

mitre.description: Only techniques the cited evidence justifies; ids from the local catalog.

items.description: an evidence_ref exactly as a tool returned it in this run, e.g. wazuh_alerts.jsonl#L64

evidence_refs.description: refs of the events that justify the technique (at least one)

unknowns.description: Answers 'what is still unknown' (question e): missing, failed or timed-out sources, open questions. Plain strings without refs. Must not be empty when correlate_evidence reports gaps.

requires_approval.description: must be true for containment (for analyst consideration; nothing is executed)
